law_name: Federal coalition agreement 2025–2029 (Arizona agreement) and government declaration
description: Agreement of about 200 pages concluded on 31 January 2025 by N-VA, MR, Les Engagés, Vooruit and CD&V under De Wever as formateur, approved by the five parties on 1–2 February 2025, and presented to the Chamber as the government declaration. It provides for a time limit on unemployment benefits, a pension bonus-malus, a 10% capital gains tax, lower taxes on work, the repeal of the nuclear phase-out law, a stricter migration policy, higher defence spending, the merger of the Brussels police zones and the abolition of the Senate.
significance: The programme of the first Belgian government led by a Flemish nationalist and the first since 2008 with a majority in both language groups.

law_name: Easter agreement (Paasakkoord): defence spending of 2% of GDP from 2025 and implementing legislation
description: Cabinet agreement of 12 April 2025 translating the coalition agreement into some 500 articles and 300 pages of legal text, according to De Wever. It added about 4 billion euros of defence spending in 2025 to reach NATO's 2% of GDP norm, partly funded from taxes on frozen Russian assets held at Euroclear (just over 1 billion euros), an exceptional 500-million-euro Belfius dividend and the reclassification of existing spending as defence, with the remainder initially unfunded; it also fixed the modalities of the unemployment-benefit time limit and of stricter asylum rules.
significance: Belgium reached 2% of GDP in defence spending in 2025 for the first time, according to NATO, up from 0.97% in 2014.

law_name: Repeal of the Act of 31 January 2003 on the phasing out of nuclear energy
description: Bill tabled by the five coalition parties and adopted by the Chamber by a large majority in May 2025, with the support of Vlaams Belang and Open VLD, against the votes of the PS, PVDA-PTB and the greens. It removes the statutory closure schedule for Belgium's reactors and the ban on building new nuclear generating capacity.
significance: Ended two decades of a legal nuclear exit; Energy Minister Mathieu Bihet called it "a turning point".

law_name: Programme Act of July 2025 (unemployment reform: benefits limited to two years)
description: Programme act adopted in plenary by the Chamber on 18 July 2025 containing the unemployment reform: from 1 January 2026, full unemployment benefits are limited to a basic 12 months plus up to 12 more depending on work record (one year for school leavers), with exceptions for people over 55 with long careers, trainees in shortage occupations, artists, dockworkers and fishermen. Existing long-term claimants are phased out in waves from January 2026.
significance: Ends Belgium's unlimited-duration unemployment benefit; about 180,000 people were expected to lose their benefit in 2026, for savings of just under 2 billion euros.

law_name: Act tightening family reunification for beneficiaries of international protection
description: Bill of Asylum and Migration Minister Anneleen Van Bossuyt (N-VA) adopted by the Chamber in the night of 17 to 18 July 2025 with the votes of the majority, Vlaams Belang and Open Vld. It raises the income requirement to 110% of the average guaranteed minimum monthly income (2,323 euros) plus 10% per additional family member, shortens the condition-free period for recognised refugees to six months, removes it for beneficiaries of subsidiary protection, lengthens waiting periods and raises the age for partner reunification to 21.
significance: Central to the government's migration policy; on 26 February 2026 the Constitutional Court suspended the stricter rules for beneficiaries of subsidiary protection, together with a law restricting reception, pending a ruling of the EU Court of Justice.

law_name: Multi-year budget agreement of 24 November 2025 (budget 2026 and trajectory to 2029)
description: Agreement reached on 24 November 2025 after the October deadlock, and presented by De Wever to the Chamber on 26 November. It aims at 9.2 billion euros a year in savings and extra revenue by 2029: indexation of wages limited to the first 4,000 euros a month in 2026 and 2028, a harmonised 12% VAT rate for hotels, takeaway meals and entertainment instead of a general VAT increase, higher excise duties on gas and lower ones on electricity, a doubled tax for people with more than 1 million euros invested in securities, a new bank levy, a 2-euro tax on parcels from outside the EU, measures to bring long-term sick people back to work, a freeze of ministers' and MPs' salaries, a 50-euro rise in the minimum wage, and an accelerated tax reform.
significance: The government's main budget package after the autumn 2025 deadlock, during which De Wever's State of the Union address was cancelled.

law_name: Capital gains tax on financial assets
description: Bill of Finance Minister Jan Jambon approved by the Federal Parliament in early April 2026, with the coalition, PS and PVDA-PTB in favour, Vlaams Belang, Anders and DéFI against and the greens abstaining. It taxes gains on the sale of financial assets at 10%, with an exemption of 10,000 euros per person (rising by 1,000 euros a year if unused, up to 15,000) and a separate regime for holders of at least 20% of a company. It has applied since 1 January 2026 under a transitional arrangement.
significance: Belgium's first general capital gains tax on financial assets, a condition of Vooruit for joining the coalition; expected yield 500 million euros a year.

law_name: Pension reform act (pension bonus-malus and career conditions)
description: Approved by the Chamber on 28 May 2026 and published in the Belgian Official Journal on 1 June 2026. It introduces a pension penalty from 2027 for people retiring early without meeting new work requirements, a new pension bonus for those working beyond the statutory age (accruing from 2026), a 156-day minimum for a year to count towards the early-retirement career condition, retirement at 60 after 42 career years of at least 234 worked days, and limits on assimilated periods of unemployment.
significance: The government's flagship structural reform alongside the unemployment-benefit limit; the target of repeated union strikes and demonstrations.

description: Bill of Finance Minister Jan Jambon adopted by the Chamber in plenary on 9 July 2026, with the majority in favour, PS, PVDA-PTB and Ecolo-Groen against and Vlaams Belang, Anders and DéFI abstaining. It raises the tax-free allowance from 10,910 euros to 14,450 euros for tax year 2030 (15,600 euros for 2031, to be confirmed by the next government), raises the work bonus for low wages, increases the exemption for the first two dependent children, phases out the marital quotient, and taxes the living wage as a replacement income.
significance: Implements the coalition's 'work must pay' pledge, phased in until 2030.

law_name: Revision of Article 195 of the Constitution (first step towards abolishing the Senate)
description: Adopted by the Senate on 3 April 2026 (36 to 8, 14 abstentions) and by the Chamber on 2 July 2026 (96 to 16, 10 abstentions). The revision adds a transitional provision allowing all Senate-related articles of the Constitution to be revised within the current legislature, instead of only after new elections.
significance: Opens the way to the planned abolition of the Senate before the 2029 elections, a reform championed by De Wever, who called the Senate a "symbol of waste"; the abolition itself still requires further two-thirds votes.
